Messages.Author: Hans Jorgen Pedersen
Messages.Body:
Hi all, I've a question for the experienced players out there.
Basically, is counterblocking possible?. Say: I take an action with on
e of my minions - my prey increases his intercept and blocks. Would it be
possible for one of my, yet untapped, minions to block the block?.

Regards
Simon Pedersen

Messages.Author: Joseph Cochran
Messages.Body:
In article <8018496...@inet.uni-c.dk>,


No. The only way to stop a block is to increase your stealth
(or play Form of Mist during combat). You can't block a block.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
js...@discus.ise.vt.edu (Joseph Cochran) writes:

>In article <8018496...@inet.uni-c.dk>,
>Hans Jorgen Pedersen <dkdf...@inet.uni-c.dk> wrote:
>>Hi all, I've a question for the experienced players out there.
>>Basically, is counterblocking possible?. Say: I take an action with on
>>e of my minions - my prey increases his intercept and blocks. Would it be
>>possible for one of my, yet untapped, minions to block the block?.

> No. The only way to stop a block is to increase your stealth
>(or play Form of Mist during combat). You can't block a block.

You could also use superior Day Operation.

Also, the DT has made it known that if you cause the blocker-to-be to become
tapped before the block resolves, then the block would be unsuccessful.

The only card capable of such an effect was the (pre-DTR 5/9/95) Anarch
Troublemaker, who could tap two minions of your Prey. If one of those
minions was the proposed blocker, then the block would be thwarted.
